head_commit.message:
test: time synchronous budgets by the fastest run; wait out chunk I/O in visual captures

Run 38032399929: Ubuntu planReader measured 245 ms against its 200 ms budget,
and visual shard 6 reported a deferred renderer that did not settle.

- planReader, scheduleClock and the journalStore warm scan (three earlier
  CI failures) compare the fastest of three timed runs with the unchanged
  budget; real latency checks keep wall time. Drilled with 250 ms of work.
- The visual capture page tracks its in-flight requests and each frozen-clock
  step first waits for them, so the 100-step bound counts page time rather
  than a busy runner's chunk I/O. A request open 15 s fails the scene.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<email-redacted>>

head_commit.message:
test: warm every own-Chrome suite once before its cases

Run 38029777462 failed one case: accountsPanel.a11y's first page-matrix case
at 5 s on hosted macOS, the same class as the estimator and m114Panel first
cases. A fresh Chrome's first page pays a renderer start and the first font
fallbacks once. Every suite that launches its own Chrome now pays it in a
beforeAll of its own via test/unit/helpers/warmBrowser.ts, so each case
keeps its deadline. Mac mini and Kubuntu: the eight files 150/150.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <<email-redacted>>
